title: Best Aesthetic Record Alternatives (October 2026)
summary: Outgrowing Aesthetic Record? We compare five alternatives on reporting, wellness and hormone charting, labs, AI scribing and pricing for growing med spas.
body_markdown:
## What Is Aesthetic Record?


Aesthetic Record is a cloud EMR and practice management platform for med spas, which[says it is trusted by more than 9,000 aesthetic clinics](https://www.aestheticrecord.com/) . It covers clinical documentation, before-and-after photo and video management, chart sign-off, online booking, memberships, inventory, two-way texting, telehealth and payments through AR Pay. It also integrates with Qualiphy for good faith exams and with a long list of third-party tools, from Mailchimp to RepeatMD.


For a practice that is mostly injectables and lasers, that is a capable product, and a lot of injectors have run on it happily for years. The friction tends to show up when the practice changes shape: a second provider, a second location, or a new service line that is more internal medicine than aesthetics.


## Why Practices Look for Aesthetic Record Alternatives


### Reports that do not add up


The complaint we hear most from Aesthetic Record owners is about financial reporting. One owner told us the numbers "don't seem to be 100% accurate," that reports cannot be customized, and that seeing the whole month means pulling three or four reports and reconciling them by hand. When the owner asked support a specific question about a report, nobody could answer it. A practice in that position is running the business on a spreadsheet built on top of the EMR, which is exactly the work the EMR was supposed to remove.


### Marketing that lives somewhere else


Re-engagement campaigns are the cheapest revenue a med spa has. A toxin patient who has not been back in 120 days is worth more than a new lead from an ad. Yet several practices described the same loop: export patients from Aesthetic Record, upload them into an email tool, send the campaign, then guess at what it produced, because nothing connects the booking back to the message. Aesthetic Record does sell LeadAR and Mailchimp and ActiveCampaign integrations, but the operators we spoke with were still doing the export by hand.


### Charting built for aesthetics first


The third reason is the one that grows over time. An owner adding hormone therapy, weight loss or primary care told us Aesthetic Record "is great for aesthetics" but weak for general health and wellness charting. Another described feeling like they needed two charting systems to get the one she wanted. Lab ordering is not among the modules Aesthetic Record lists on its product page, which matters once you are drawing testosterone, A1C and lipid panels every few months.


### Costs that grow with headcount


Aesthetic Record's[published pricing](https://www.aestheticrecord.com/pricing) is per user: $15 per user per month on Essentials and $19 on Accelerator, plus a $399 startup fee. ChartSmart AI runs $30 to $75 a month depending on chart volume, cloud e-prescribing is billed per prescriber, and two-way texting and several integrations sit in the higher tier. None of that is unusual, but it means the sticker price and the real monthly bill can be far apart. Our[clinic software cost breakdown](https://decodahealth.com/blog/clinic-software-cost-breakdown) walks through how to compare quotes that are structured differently.


## How We Ranked These Aesthetic Record Alternatives


We scored each platform on the gaps above rather than on generic feature counts:


- **Reporting you can trust:** can an owner see revenue by provider, service and location without reconciling exports?
- **Charting beyond aesthetics:** does it handle hormones, weight loss, IV and wellness as well as injectables?
- **Labs:** can you order, receive and trend labs inside the chart?
- **Marketing tied to revenue:** can you target lapsed patients and see what each campaign booked?
- **Payments:** will it process GLP-1s, peptides and HRT without holds?
- **Switching cost:** who does the migration, and how long does it take?


Vendor details come from each company's own site and from our earlier comparisons of[medspa EHR software](https://decodahealth.com/blog/top-medspa-ehr-software) and[Boulevard alternatives](https://decodahealth.com/blog/boulevard-software-alternatives) . Where a vendor does not publish something, the table says so rather than guessing.

On the reporting complaint,[Decoda's analytics](https://decodahealth.com/products/analytics) filter revenue, provider performance, patients and appointments by date range, location or provider, and let you drill from a summary line into the transactions behind it. On marketing, campaigns target patient cohorts straight from the record, so a list of toxin patients overdue by 120 days is a filter, not an export. Revenue is attributed from the appointment the campaign produced. We cover the approach in more depth in our guide to[med spa cohort targeting and re-engagement](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-cohort-targeting-re-engagement) .


The rest of the platform covers the services Aesthetic Record practices tend to add next:

- Inventory that deducts units at the point of charting
- An AI front desk that answers calls and texts, checks real availability and books, reschedules or cancels the appointment itself

Switching is the part owners worry about most, and fairly so. Decoda runs the migration itself and finishes in 3-4 weeks, guaranteed. Our[guide to what transfers in a med spa EMR migration](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-emr-migration-what-transfers) lists the records to check before you sign anything.


**Best for:** independent practices with one to 20 locations that run aesthetics alongside wellness, weight loss, hormone, IV or longevity services, and owners who want reporting they do not have to reconcile.


## PatientNow


### What They Offer


PatientNow is an aesthetic EMR centered on app-based photo documentation and before-and-after tracking, with patient communication, automated follow-up and practice reporting for single and multi-location aesthetic practices. Its AI came through the acquisition of Recura AI in late 2025, so it runs on top of the existing product rather than through it.


For a mature aesthetic practice whose main workflow is photo documentation, it is a reasonable lateral move from Aesthetic Record. It is a weaker fit for practices building hormone or longevity programs, where membership billing and lab trending carry more weight.


**Best for:** established aesthetic practices that live in before-and-after photos and do not need complex memberships.


## AestheticsPro


### What They Offer


AestheticsPro is one of the longest-running medspa platforms, with EMR, scheduling, consent forms and point of sale. It shows up at or near the top of most review-site lists of Aesthetic Record alternatives, including[GetApp's Aesthetic Record page](https://www.getapp.com/medical-lab-software/a/aesthetic-record/) . Recurring complaints include online booking failures that leave staff calling patients to correct appointments, and post-appointment texts that do not always send.


**Best for:** aesthetic practices that want a familiar, established tool and are not adding clinical service lines.


## Zenoti


### What They Offer


Zenoti is broad multi-location spa and medspa software with scheduling, marketing and reporting that hold up at enterprise scale. Its AI scribe is a separately priced add-on, data exports carry a fee, and support turnaround is measured in weeks rather than hours. The operational depth is real, but it assumes someone on staff whose job is running the software.


**Best for:** large chains and franchises with dedicated operations teams.


## Mangomint


### What They Offer


Mangomint is polished salon and spa booking software that moved to a single flat price of $120 per location per month plus $10 per user per month in August 2026. It has no clinical documentation, no EMR and no high-risk payment processing. Some owners shortlist it because it is easy to use, but leaving Aesthetic Record for Mangomint means adding a separate EMR, which recreates the two-system problem many are trying to escape. We cover it in more detail in our[Mangomint comparison](https://decodahealth.com/blog/best-mangomint-alternative-elective-care) .


**Best for:** non-medical spas and beauty businesses without clinical requirements.

## What to Ask Before You Switch


Whichever platform you shortlist, the demo will look good. These questions tell you more than the demo does:


- **Show me last month's revenue by provider.** Ask to see it built live from sample data, then ask how you would answer a question the standard report does not cover.
- **What exactly transfers?** Charts and photos are the easy part. Prepaid packages, membership balances and gift cards are where migrations quietly lose money, and one practice we spoke with still runs its old point of sale because packages never made it across.
- **Who does the migration, and is there a fee?** Get the timeline in writing.
- **What does a hormone or GLP-1 follow-up look like in the chart?** If the answer is a generic template, expect to build it yourself.
- **Which of my services will your processor refuse or hold?** Name them: semaglutide, peptides, testosterone.
- **What does my bill look like with every add-on I need?** Ask for a quote that includes AI charting, e-prescribing, texting volume and integrations.


Contract timing matters too. Several owners told us their switch date was set by an annual contract or by a medical director who requires every provider under them to use the same EMR. Find out both before you start evaluating, so the decision is not made for you.


## Final Thoughts on Choosing an Aesthetic Record Alternative


If your practice is aesthetics-only and the reports reconcile, Aesthetic Record may still be the right tool, and switching for its own sake is rarely worth the disruption. The practices that should move are the ones that have changed shape: adding hormones, weight loss, IV or longevity care, running a second provider or location, or spending hours each month rebuilding numbers the software should already have. ## Frequently Asked Questions


What is the best Aesthetic Record alternative for a med spa adding wellness services?


If you are adding weight loss, hormone therapy, IV or longevity services, look for a platform that charts those services as well as it charts injectables and that orders and trends labs inside the chart. Decoda Health covers aesthetics, wellness, labs and payments in one system, which is why it ranks first on this list for practices making that move.


How much does Aesthetic Record cost?


Aesthetic Record publishes per-user pricing: $15 per user per month on Essentials and $19 per user per month on Accelerator, each with a $399 startup fee, and Enterprise is quoted. ChartSmart AI, e-prescribing and LeadAR are priced separately, so check its pricing page for the add-ons your practice would need.


Why do practices switch away from Aesthetic Record?


The reasons we hear most often are financial reports that are hard to reconcile or customize, marketing that requires exporting patient lists into a separate email tool, and charting that fits aesthetics better than general health, hormones or weight loss. Practices that are purely aesthetic and happy with their reporting often have no reason to move.


Can I move my charts and photos out of Aesthetic Record?


Yes, but ask any new vendor exactly what transfers and who does the work. Patient demographics, chart history, photos, consents, package balances and membership status all need a plan. Decoda runs the migration itself and finishes in 3-4 weeks, guaranteed.


Is there an Aesthetic Record alternative with lab ordering built in?


Lab ordering is not among the modules Aesthetic Record lists on its product page. Decoda Health orders Quest and LabCorp panels from the chart, matches results to the patient automatically and trends values over time, which matters most for hormone, weight loss and longevity programs.


Which Aesthetic Record alternatives handle high-risk payments like GLP-1s and peptides?


Mainstream processors often flag peptide and semaglutide sales and hold funds for review. Decoda Health processes injectables, weight-loss drugs, IV therapy, HRT and PRP through payment processing built for those services. Mangomint does not offer high-risk processing, so confirm this with any vendor before you sign.
